vulnerable.title: Read another tenant's member profiles
vulnerable.intent: A member of Harbor Logistics asks the API for the profile rows belonging to Northwind Analytics.
vulnerable.sql_text:
select id, tenant_id, full_name, job_title
   from synthetic.profiles
  where tenant_id = '11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111'
  order by full_name
vulnerable.actor_label: Priya Raghavan · member of Harbor Logistics
vulnerable.consequence: Every customer of the platform could read the names, roles, and contact records of every other customer.

vulnerable.title: Read the member's own tenant profiles
vulnerable.intent: The same member asks for the profiles that belong to their own tenant. This confirms the policy constrains the boundary without breaking the product.
vulnerable.sql_text:
select id, tenant_id, full_name, job_title
   from synthetic.profiles
  where tenant_id = '22222222-2222-4222-8222-222222222222'
  order by full_name
vulnerable.actor_label: Priya Raghavan · member of Harbor Logistics
vulnerable.consequence: If this path is blocked, the fix has broken legitimate access rather than closed the boundary.

vulnerable.title: Modify another tenant's member profile
vulnerable.intent: The member attempts to write to a Northwind profile row.
vulnerable.sql_text:
update synthetic.profiles
      set job_title = 'Edited from another tenant'
    where tenant_id = '11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111'
vulnerable.verify_sql:
select id, tenant_id, full_name, job_title
      from synthetic.profiles
     where tenant_id = '11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111'
     order by full_name
vulnerable.actor_label: Priya Raghavan · member of Harbor Logistics
vulnerable.consequence: A tenant could silently alter another tenant's records, with no audit trail on the victim's side.

      and full_name = 'Taylor Kim'
vulnerable.verify_sql:

      from synthetic.profiles
     where tenant_id = '11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111'

vulnerable.actor_label: Priya Raghavan · member of Harbor Logistics

vulnerable.title: Enumerate another tenant's membership

   from synthetic.org_members
  where tenant_id = '11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111'

vulnerable.actor_label: Priya Raghavan · member of Harbor Logistics

vulnerable.title: Move the member's own record into another tenant
vulnerable.intent: The member updates a row they are allowed to read and writes a different tenant_id into it, granting themselves standing membership of another tenant. Reproducing this needs both a permissive read policy and a widened write check: PostgreSQL tests the new row against the SELECT policy as well.
vulnerable.sql_text:
update synthetic.org_members
      set tenant_id = '11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111'
    where profile_id = '5c1d8b22-0002-4000-8000-000000000003'
vulnerable.verify_sql:
select id, tenant_id, profile_id, member_role
      from synthetic.org_members
     where profile_id = '5c1d8b22-0002-4000-8000-000000000003'
vulnerable.actor_label: Priya Raghavan · member of Harbor Logistics
vulnerable.consequence: A member could grant themselves standing membership of another tenant, turning a read boundary into a persistent account takeover.

vulnerable.title: Write a new object as an anonymous visitor
vulnerable.intent: An unauthenticated caller attempts to add a row to the object table.
vulnerable.sql_text:
insert into synthetic.storage_objects (id, tenant_id, bucket_id, object_path, visibility, byte_size)
   values ('f0000009-0009-4000-8000-000000000009',
           '11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111',
           'tenant-documents', 'northwind/uploaded-by-anonymous.txt', 'private', 12)
vulnerable.verify_sql:
select id, tenant_id, bucket_id, object_path
      from synthetic.storage_objects
     where object_path = 'northwind/uploaded-by-anonymous.txt'
vulnerable.consequence: An anonymous caller could plant files inside a customer's bucket, which is both a storage-cost and a content-trust problem.

vulnerable.title: Find exposed tables with row level security switched off
vulnerable.intent: A catalog inspection listing every fixture table that is reachable through a role grant but has no row level security enabled. An empty result is the expected state.
vulnerable.sql_text:
select 'synthetic.' || c.relname as relation,
          c.relrowsecurity          as row_security_enabled
     from pg_catalog.pg_class c
     join pg_catalog.pg_namespace n on n.oid = c.relnamespace
    where n.nspname = 'synthetic'
      and c.relkind = 'r'
      and c.relname in ('profiles', 'org_members', 'invoices', 'storage_objects')
      and not c.relrowsecurity
    order by 1
vulnerable.consequence: A table exposed by a grant with row level security switched off consults no policy at all, so the project looks protected in the dashboard while returning every row.

vulnerable.title: Find write privileges held by the anonymous role
vulnerable.intent: A catalog inspection listing every insert, update, or delete privilege granted to the anonymous role. An empty result is the expected state.
vulnerable.sql_text:
select g.table_schema || '.' || g.table_name as relation,
          g.grantee,
          lower(g.privilege_type)               as privilege
     from information_schema.role_table_grants g
    where g.table_schema = 'synthetic'
      and g.grantee = 'anon'
      and g.privilege_type in ('INSERT', 'UPDATE', 'DELETE')
    order by 1, 3
vulnerable.consequence: A write privilege on the anonymous role lets an unauthenticated caller change stored data regardless of how carefully the read policies were written.

vulnerable.title: Find policies whose predicate is unconditional
vulnerable.intent: A catalog inspection listing every policy on a fixture table whose USING or WITH CHECK expression is the literal true. Such a policy satisfies the row level security requirement without constraining anything. An empty result is the expected state.
vulnerable.sql_text:
select 'synthetic.' || c.relname as relation,
          p.polname                 as policy_name,
          case when pg_catalog.pg_get_expr(p.polqual, p.polrelid) = 'true'
               then 'using' else 'with check' end as unconditional_clause
     from pg_catalog.pg_policy p
     join pg_catalog.pg_class c on c.oid = p.polrelid
     join pg_catalog.pg_namespace n on n.oid = c.relnamespace
    where n.nspname = 'synthetic'
      and c.relname in ('profiles', 'org_members', 'invoices', 'storage_objects')
      and (pg_catalog.pg_get_expr(p.polqual, p.polrelid) = 'true'
        or pg_catalog.pg_get_expr(p.polwithcheck, p.polrelid) = 'true')
    order by 1, 2
vulnerable.consequence: A policy that reads using (true) makes the dashboard report row level security as enabled while every row remains readable. It is the failure that most often survives a launch review.
